correctness.rationale: For each ridge, solving the positive-definite 2x2 facet-normal Gram system gives two disjoint necessary failures. The Dirichlet exponential representation evaluates their exact probabilities. Nonpositive cross products ensure sufficient feasibility; the Stieltjes inverse argument supplies all face normals for globally nonobtuse simplices. A one-shear simplex has a unique obtuse pair and attains ridge-probability equality. The proof and deterministic checker establish the stated ranges and limits.

The quantitative all-dimensional Q_{ij} bound with its equality regime is a genuinely additional assertion not implied by qualitative equality or existence theorems.

value.rationale: A natural face-specific active-region volume, motivated by mean numbers of concurrent normals, has a sharp analytic bound depending only on an obtuse dihedral cosine and two vertex altitudes. It yields an all-dimensional strictly positive mean-normal deficit and a solved family of geometrically simple extremizers with cubic degenerating visibility. This is a motivated structural refinement, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
